title: Automation, Commissioning, Reliability & Failure Response
level: Environmental, Irrigation & Fertigation Systems Specialist / advanced specialization development
intendedAudience: Cultivation personnel responsible for commissioning checks, controller/alarm verification, system reliability evidence and safe failure-response handoff
prerequisites: Completion of EIFS Courses 1-7 or equivalent advanced environmental/irrigation systems preparation
evidencePolicy: Course reuses governed sensor/data-quality, environmental, irrigation, safety and data-integrity evidence. Commissioning and reliability claims are framed as verification workflows; exact controller logic, electrical design, network/security configuration and protected service procedures remain facility/vendor/qualified-role specific.
assessmentPolicy: Development-only until technical/assessment review, accessibility review and pilot evidence are complete. Course completion does not authorize control-program changes, electrical work, alarm/interlock bypass, compressed-gas service or protected equipment repair.
description: Develops specialist verification of automated cultivation systems from commissioning through normal operation, degraded modes, alarm/interlock response, failure classification, recovery verification and qualified handoff.
learningOutcomes: Build a commissioning verification plan that checks sensor identity, controller inputs/outputs, alarm/interlock behavior, command-versus-response and representative crop-zone outcomes before operational acceptance.

Differentiate normal control variation, sensor/data-quality faults, communication failures, equipment non-response and capacity/sequence limitations using converging evidence rather than controller status alone.
Evaluate fail-safe, degraded-mode and fallback responses for environmental and irrigation failures while preserving life-safety, crop-protection and role-authority boundaries.

Verify restoration after corrective action using comparable pre/post measurements, alarm history, command-response evidence and defined acceptance criteria rather than assuming repair completion equals recovery.

Produce a commissioning or failure-response packet that another qualified responder can reconstruct, including system identity, baseline, fault evidence, safe-state actions, unresolved risk and next authorized role.
